questions.question: Which statement correctly describes an electrophile? Options: A accepts a pair of electrons; B always negative; C always positive; D donates a pair of electrons.
steps: An electrophile is an electron-pair acceptor, so it is attracted to electron-rich sites.
B is wrong: electrophiles can be neutral (e.g. BF3) or positive, not always negative.
C is wrong: electrophiles are not always positive, since BF3 is neutral.
D describes a nucleophile, which donates a lone pair, so it is wrong.
Answer A.

questions.question: For the process H2O -> H+ + OH-, what type of bond breaking occurs? Options: A electrophilic; B heterolytic; C homolytic; D ionic.
steps: In H2O -> H+ + OH-, the O-H bond breaks and forms ions.
Both electrons of the bond go to the oxygen atom, leaving H+ with none.
When one atom takes both electrons of the bond, the fission is heterolytic.
Homolytic fission gives radicals, not ions, and electrophilic and ionic are not types of bond breaking here.
Answer B.

questions.question: What is the molecular formula of the compound shown? Options: A C2HO2; B C4H2O4; C C4H4O4; D C4H6O4.
steps: The ring is a four-membered carbon ring (cyclobutene) with 4 carbon atoms, so C4.
The two ring carbons carrying O are C=O (carbonyl) with no H, and the two ring carbons joined by the C=C each carry an OH, so there are no H on the ring.
The only hydrogens are the two in the two OH groups, so H2.
Oxygens: 2 C=O + 2 OH = 4, so the formula is C4H2O4 (option B).

questions.question: A sequence of four molecules is shown. Give the molecular formula of the fifth molecule. Options: A CH4O; B C6H11O; C C6H14O; D C7H16O.
steps: The molecules are ethanol (C2H6O), propan-2-ol (C3H8O), butan-2-ol (C4H10O) and pentan-2-ol (C5H12O).
Each step adds one CH2 group, so the pattern is a homologous series of secondary alcohols with OH on carbon 2.
The fifth member is hexan-2-ol with six carbons: C6H14O (option C).
Check with the general formula CnH(2n+2)O: n = 6 gives C6H14O.

questions.question: What is the name of this type of sequence? Options: A functional group; B homologous series; C homolytic series; D skeletal formulae.
steps: Consecutive members of the sequence differ by one CH2 unit.
Members share the same general formula and the same functional group.
They have similar chemical properties and a gradual change in physical properties.
This family of compounds is a homologous series, so the answer is B.

questions.question: Write a balanced equation for the thermal decomposition of (NH4)2Cr2O7 at about 180 deg C, giving an oxide of chromium, nitrogen and water as the only products.
steps: Products are Cr2O3 (oxide of chromium), N2 (nitrogen) and H2O (water).
N: 2 on the left, so 1 N2 on the right.
Cr: 2 on the left, so 1 Cr2O3 on the right.
H: 8 on the left, so 4 H2O on the right (4 x 2 = 8 H).
O: 7 on the left (7 O in the salt), and 3 + 4 = 7 on the right, so the equation balances.

questions.question: Give a name for the type of reaction in part (a)(i).
questions.answer: Thermal decomposition (it is also a redox reaction)
steps: One compound breaks down into simpler products when heated, which is thermal decomposition.
Cr falls from +6 to +3 in Cr2O3, so it is reduced.
N rises from -3 in NH4+ to 0 in N2, so it is oxidised.
The reaction is therefore also a redox reaction.

questions.question: 0.00100 mol of (NH4)2Cr2O7 is heated and 25.2 cm^3 of N2 is formed at laboratory temperature. Using pressure 101 kPa and PV = nRT, find the laboratory temperature in deg C.
steps: From the equation, 1 mol of (NH4)2Cr2O7 gives 1 mol of N2, so n(N2) = 0.00100 mol.
Convert pressure: 101 kPa = 101000 Pa.
Convert to Celsius: 306 - 273 = 33 deg C.

questions.question: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram of the ammonium ion, using dots for nitrogen electrons and crosses for hydrogen electrons.
questions.answer: Nitrogen at the centre with four N-H single bonds; each bond is one shared pair (one dot from N, one cross from H); no lone pair on N; whole ion in square brackets with +.
steps: Nitrogen has 5 outer electrons and each hydrogen has 1, so the total is 9, and the +1 charge removes one, leaving 8.
Those 8 electrons form four N-H bonds, so there are four shared pairs.
Each bond is shown as one dot (from N) and one cross (from H).
N has no lone pair in NH4+, so there are no extra dots on nitrogen.
Enclose the ion in square brackets and write + at the top right.

questions.question: Explain the shape of the ammonium ion using electron-pair repulsion theory.
questions.answer: Tetrahedral: four bonding pairs and no lone pairs repel equally, giving bond angles of 109.5 deg.
steps: The central N atom has four bonding pairs of electrons and no lone pairs.
Electron pairs repel each other and move as far apart as possible to minimise repulsion.
Four equal repulsions give a tetrahedral arrangement.
The H-N-H bond angles are 109.5 deg.

questions.question: Tick the hazard symbols that apply to ammonium dichromate(VI) from the symbols shown on the packaging.
questions.answer: Tick the oxidising (flame over circle), toxic (skull and crossbones) and corrosive symbols.
steps: Match each warning on the packaging to a hazard symbol.
"Strong oxidiser that enhances the combustion of other substances": the flame over circle (oxidising) symbol.
"Toxic when inhaled and through the skin": the skull and crossbones symbol.

"Contact can irritate and burn the skin and eyes, with possible eye damage": the corrosive symbol (liquid eating a hand and a surface); the exclamation mark would only be for irritation, and burning is more severe.
The plain flame (flammable) and exploding bomb symbols are not stated on the packaging, so they are not ticked.

questions.question: Suggest why ammonium dichromate(VI) must not be stored in the same cupboard as alkanes.
questions.answer: Ammonium dichromate(VI) is an oxidising agent and alkanes are flammable, so storing them together could cause a fire or explosion.
steps: Ammonium dichromate(VI) contains Cr(VI) and acts as an oxidising agent.
Alkanes are flammable and are oxidised readily.
If the two are stored together, a leak or spill could let them react.
The reaction could start a fire or explosion, so they must be kept apart.

questions.question: Give the IUPAC name of the alkane shown. Options: A 2-ethyl-4,5-dimethylheptane; B 6-ethyl-3,4-dimethylheptane; C 3,4,6-trimethyloctane; D 3,5,6-trimethyloctane.
steps: Find the longest carbon chain: it runs from the right-hand end along the zig-zag and then down through the two carbons of the lower-left branch, giving 8 carbons. So the parent is octane, and the lower-left branch is part of the chain, not an ethyl group.
Three one-carbon branches (methyl groups) hang off this chain, so it is a trimethyloctane.
Number from the right-hand end: the methyls are on carbons 3, 4 and 6. Numbering from the other end gives 3, 5, 6, which is higher at the second locant.
The lowest locants are 3,4,6, so the name is 3,4,6-trimethyloctane (option C).

questions.question: A substance is labelled with a hazard symbol (image, not in text). What does the symbol mean? Options: A gloves must be worn; B corrosive; C do not store with flammable substances; D oxidising.
steps: The symbol shows a liquid dripping onto a hand and a surface, which is the GHS corrosive symbol.
Oxidising is a flame over a circle, and flammable is a plain flame, so the other options do not match.

questions.question: What do heterolytic fission products consist of? Options: A free radicals only; B ions only; C free radicals and positive ions only; D free radicals and negative ions only.
steps: Heterolytic fission: both electrons of the bond go to one atom.
This gives a positive ion (cation) and a negative ion (anion).
Free radicals form only in homolytic fission, where each atom gets one electron.
So heterolytic fission produces ions only, answer B.

questions.question: What is the name of a series such as the one shown? Options: A addition; B heterolytic; C homologous; D homolytic.
steps: A homologous series is a family of compounds with the same general formula and functional group.
Members differ by CH2 and show a gradual change in physical properties.
Addition, heterolytic and homolytic describe reaction or bond types, not families of compounds.
Answer C.

questions.question: Which skeletal structure matches 3,4-dichloro-2,2-dimethylpentane? The options are skeletal structures (images) not in the text.
steps: Draw the carbon skeleton: pentane chain C1 to C5, with two CH3 groups on C2, and one Cl on each of C3 and C4.
Structure A is (CH3)3C-CHCl-CHCl-CH3: a quaternary carbon (C2) carrying two methyl branches plus C1, then two CHCl carbons (C3 and C4), then a terminal CH3 (C5).
B, C and D each put a Cl on the quaternary carbon, which should carry the two methyls, so none of them fits.
Only A gives 3,4-dichloro-2,2-dimethylpentane.

questions.question: Four reagent bottles W, X, Y and Z have hazard labels (images, not in text). Which two should never be stored together? Options: A W and Z; B Y and Z; C W and X; D Y and X.
steps: Read the labels: W is oxidising (flame over circle), X is flammable (flame), Y is corrosive and Z is toxic (skull and crossbones).
Oxidising agents supply oxygen and make flammable materials burn much more readily, so an oxidiser and a flammable substance must never be stored together.
That pair is W and X, so the answer is C.

questions.question: Prop-2-en-1-ol is flammable, toxic and an environmental hazard. Which hazard symbols should be on its container? The options are symbol images not in the text.
questions.answer: A: flame, skull and crossbones, environmental hazard
steps: Flammable corresponds to the plain flame symbol.
Toxic corresponds to the skull and crossbones symbol.
Environmental hazard corresponds to the dead tree and fish symbol.
Only option A has all three: B and C contain an oxidising symbol, and B and D contain the health-hazard symbol, which is not a stated hazard.

questions.question: What is the empirical formula of the molecule shown? Options: A C4H4Cl; B C4H7Cl; C C8H11Cl2; D C8H14Cl2.
steps: Count the atoms: a six-carbon saturated ring, plus one CH3 and one CH2Cl, so 8 carbons in total.
Hydrogens: the ring has three CH2 (6 H) and three CH (3 H), so 9 H; the CH3 adds 3 and the CH2Cl adds 2, giving 14 H.
Two chlorines (one on the ring, one in CH2Cl), so the molecular formula is C8H14Cl2.
Divide by 2 for the simplest whole-number ratio: C4H7Cl (option B).

questions.question: What is the IUPAC name of the hydrocarbon shown? Options: A 2-ethyl-3-methylnonane; B 3,4-dimethyldecane; C 8-ethyl-7-methylnonane; D 7,8-dimethyldecane.
steps: The longest chain goes from the left end along the zig-zag to the carbon carrying the ethyl group and on through the ethyl group, giving 10 carbons, so the parent is decane (not nonane).
The branches are two methyl groups on adjacent carbons: one on the carbon where the ethyl group joins the chain, and one on the next carbon along.
Number from the ethyl end so the methyls are on the lowest locants: 3 and 4 (the other direction would give 7 and 8).
The name is 3,4-dimethyldecane (option B).

questions.question: Which hazard warning symbol would be found on a bottle of hexane? The symbol options are images not in the text.
steps: Hexane is a volatile alkane that catches fire easily, so it is highly flammable.
The flame symbol (A) is the flammable pictogram; B is oxidising, C is corrosive, D is toxic.

questions.question: Hydrogen peroxide solution causes serious eye damage, is harmful if swallowed and is an oxidising agent. Which hazard symbols should be on its containers? The symbols are images not in the text.
questions.answer: A: corrosive, exclamation mark (harmful) and oxidising
steps: Serious eye damage: corrosive symbol.
Harmful if swallowed: exclamation mark symbol (harmful or irritant).
Oxidising agent: flame over circle symbol.
Only option A contains corrosive, exclamation mark and oxidising together.

questions.question: In an experiment using hydrogen peroxide to measure rate of decomposition, which of these reduce the risk: (I) an alternative method with less hazardous materials, (II) working on a smaller scale, (III) taking precautions specific to the hazard? Options: A (I) only; B (III) only; C (II) and (III); D (I), (II) and (III).
steps: (I) An alternative method with less hazardous materials removes the hazard at source.
(II) A smaller scale reduces the amount of hazardous material used and the exposure risk.
(III) Precautions specific to the hazard, such as eye protection, reduce the risk directly.
All three reduce risk, so the answer is D.
